title: Parse repository references
acceptance: Given owner/name or a GitHub URL (optionally with a branch), then the owner, repo and ref are extracted; other hosts are rejected.

title: Select indexable files
acceptance: Given a repository tree, then lockfiles, vendored and generated files, binaries and oversized files are excluded and README and docs rank first, capped at 120 files.

title: Chunking
acceptance: Given a file, then overlapping line windows keep original line numbers and Markdown breaks on headings.

title: Local embeddings and retrieval
acceptance: Given indexed chunks and a question, then the most similar chunks are returned with at most two per file.
evidence: PR 1: ranking and diversity tests; real run on sindresorhus/ky indexed 93 files into 475 chunks and returned the test files for a testing question.

title: Cited answers
status: Implemented, not verified end to end
acceptance: Given retrieved sources and a key, then the model is instructed to answer only from them and cite as [n]; citations map to sources.
Given no key, then retrieval results are still shown.
evidence: PR 1: prompt and citation tests. Written answer verified with a scripted model reply, not a real provider.

title: Code viewer synced to citations
acceptance: Given an answer with citations, when the user picks one, then the viewer opens that file, scrolls to the lines and highlights them.
evidence: manual: PR 2, in Chrome citation 1 opened readme.md and citation 2 switched to test/type-guards.ts with its lines highlighted.

title: Provider key kept in the session by default
status: Implemented, not verified end to end
acceptance: Given a provider key, then it is kept in sessionStorage for the tab by default, kept on the device only when the user ticks "Remember on this device", and removable with "Clear key"; the provider choice persists.
evidence: Key store tests; typecheck and build (SEC-002). Not exercised in a browser because the app needs a model download that awaits the user's permission.

title: Product analytics without user data
status: Implemented, not verified end to end
acceptance: Given no NEXT_PUBLIC_POSTHOG_KEY at build time, then no script loaded on page view contains the analytics SDK, no analytics request is made and nothing is logged.

Given a key, then the app captures only $pageview (on load and on route change), index_built (chunk_bucket, duration_ms) when an index finishes, and repo_asked (repo as the public owner/name, question_length_bucket) when a question is submitted; every event carries app: "repoask" and surface: "web".
Given any event, then it carries no question text, repository content, answer, prompt, provider key, name, email or file path; sizes travel as coarse buckets.

Given a Node host and a key, then analytics requests go to this origin under /ingest and are proxied to PostHog's ingestion hosts only; given the static export, then they go to the host named in NEXT_PUBLIC_POSTHOG_HOST.

Given no key, then the /ingest route is not registered: a request to /ingest/* on a Node host returns 404 and is not forwarded anywhere. A rewrite is a server-side route that exists whether or not a client calls it, so an ungated one would relay any request body to PostHog's public ingestion API from this origin.
Given a browser that sends Do Not Track, then nothing is captured.
evidence: PR 24: bucket tests and the no-browser no-op test. manual: with no key, the Node build and the GitHub Pages export were built and `grep -rli posthog` over .next/static and out/ found nothing, and none of the 8 scripts the page references mentions it; with a placeholder key the 315 KB SDK chunk exists but no page HTML references it, and the three /ingest rewrites are emitted. PR 25, proxy gate: `tests/ingest-proxy.test.ts` imports the real `next.config.ts` and calls its `rewrites()` with the key unset, empty and set, and under the static export; it was run against the ungated config and failed. manual: with no key, `.next/routes-manifest.json` lists no rewrites and on `next start` `POST /ingest/e/` and `GET /ingest/static/array.js` return 404; with a throwaway key the manifest lists the three rewrites (no request was sent to PostHog). Not exercised against a PostHog project because no token was available, so event delivery is unverified.
